summary: The combined project-owned reference finally produced a rendered Stegosaurus candidate where broad dorsal plates and a visible four-spike thagomizer are present in the same app-facing image. The best route was low-weight IP-Adapter style transfer from the prior tail-room candidate plus moderate ControlNet strength from the combined plate/thagomizer guide. Direct low-denoise i2i preserved the guide too literally, while stronger ControlNet made the body and plate bases more shell-like.
primaryRejectReasons: direct i2i outputs remain too flat and guide-like for app use
low ControlNet strength makes plates less reliable or keeps older rounded/decorative reads
high ControlNet strength improves plate and tail-spike count but can turn the torso into a shell-like body
selected output still needs body, limb placement, and plate-base review before approval
usefulFindings: The combined plate/thagomizer reference is a better ControlNet source than separate plate-only or tail-only guides.
For Stegosaurus, IP weight around 0.07 and ControlNet strength around 0.72 preserved more natural texture while keeping the four-spike thagomizer visible.
This output is useful for app comparison and user feedback, but it should stay out of train_seed until torso shape and limb placement are corrected.
nextRoute: Use the selected app candidate as a visual feedback target only. For production quality, continue toward a Stegosaurus-compatible LoRA or a reviewed synthetic expansion that preserves broad separated plates without shell-like torso drift.
